expansion hover

An APIVoid v2 API key with 2 credits for domain lookups or 1 credit for email verification

This module queries APIVoid v2 for DNS records and SSL certificates of domains and hostnames, or verifies email addresses. Results are returned as MISP objects. AS
Expansion

AssemblyLine Query

assemblyline_query

A module to query the AssemblyLine API with a submission ID to get the submission report and parse it.

Module details
Module Type
expansion
Input
Link of an AssemblyLine submission report.
Output
MISP attributes & objects parsed from the AssemblyLine submission.
Features
The module requires the address of the AssemblyLine server you want to query as well as your credentials used for this instance. Credentials include the used-ID and an API key or the password associated to the user-ID. The submission ID extracted from the submission link is then used to query AssemblyLine and get the full submission report. This report is parsed to extract file objects and the associated IPs, domains or URLs the files are connecting to. Some more data may be parsed in the future. The optional debug flag logs the full parsed MISP event, including indicators and classification tags, to the service logger. It is disabled by default. See https://github.com/MISP/misp-modules/blob/main/documentation/expansion/assemblyline_query.md.
References
https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/assemblyline
Author
Christian Studer

AU
Import

Autopsy and Mobile Forensic Selected Results Import

autopsy_import

Import selected browser, download, communication and application artifacts with forensic provenance.

Module details
Module Type
import
Input
Base64 UTF-8 Autopsy selected-row CSV or misp-forensic-selected version 1 JSON.
Output
Source report, forensic-artifact provenance and linked tsk-* or software observations.
Requirements
PyMISP
Features
Accepts Autopsy Export Selected Rows to CSV and a versioned selected-results JSON interchange for mobile parsers. Reuses tsk-web-history/bookmark/cookie/search-query/downloads, tsk-chats and software objects. Preserves selected raw rows, report hashes and case/device/source identifiers in forensic-artifact objects. Explicit row selection omits the full source attachment when rows are excluded. All attributes are unreviewed, non-IDS and non-correlating. Local timestamps need an explicit report offset; paths and URLs are never opened. Commercial native reports require sample fixtures and a named maintainer before an adapter is added. See the [usage guide](https://github.com/MISP/misp-modules/blob/main/documentation/import_mod/autopsy_import.md).
References
https://www.autopsy.com/ https://github.com/sleuthkit/autopsy/blob/develop/Core/src/org/sleuthkit/autopsy/directorytree/ExportCSVAction.java

MISP Project

Module details
Module Type
export
Input
MISP events and object attributes in standard, bare or legacy export format.
Output
Base64-encoded libpcap capture filter for tcpdump -F; skipped counts and warnings in the API response.
Features
Produces a sorted, deduplicated BPF capture expression for IPv4/IPv6 hosts and networks, IP/port pairs, domains, hostname/port pairs, domain/IP pairs, ports and MAC addresses. Only to_ids attributes are included; deleted data is excluded. Names are resolved by libpcap at filter compilation time. Empty matches return an error rather than an unfiltered capture. MISP events and object attributes in standard, bare or legacy export format.
Output
Base64-encoded IOS/IOS-XE ACL configuration fragments; skipped counts and integration warnings.
Features
Exports validated event and object network attributes as named IPv4 extended and IPv6 ACL fragments. Defaults to deny entries; mode=log emits permit entries with log. Cisco ACL logging is first-match and permits matching traffic, so it cannot preserve later deny decisions. Only to_ids attributes are included; deleted data is excluded. DNS-only attributes require opt-in resolve_dns. See the [usage guide](https://github.com/MISP/misp-modules/blob/main/documentation/export_mod/cisco_acl_export.md).
References

Import

CSV Import

csvimport

Import MISP attributes from base64-encoded UTF-8 CSV contents.

Module details
Module Type
import
Input
Base64-encoded UTF-8 CSV contents in the JSON data field.
Output
MISP Event attributes
Requirements
PyMISP
Features
In order to parse data from a csv file, a header is required to let the module know which column is matching with known attribute fields / MISP types. This header either comes from the csv file itself or is part of the configuration of the module and should be filled out in MISP plugin settings, each field separated by COMMAS. Fields that do not match with any type known in MISP or are not MISP attribute fields should be ignored in import, using a space or simply nothing between two separators (example: 'ip-src, , comment, '). If the csv file already contains a header that does not start by a '#', you should tick the checkbox 'has_header' to avoid importing it and have potential issues. You can also redefine the header even if it is already contained in the file, by following the rules for headers explained earlier. One reason why you would redefine a header is for instance when you want to skip some fields, or some fields are not valid types. For REST API requests, put the base64-encoded UTF-8 CSV contents in data; file is not a server-side path to read. See the [REST API guide](https://github.com/MISP/misp-modules/blob/main/documentation/import_mod/csvimport.md).
References
https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4180 https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7111

DMARC Import

dmarc_import

Import DMARC aggregate XML reports, including gzip and ZIP files.

Module details
Module Type
import
Input
DMARC aggregate XML, optionally gzip- or ZIP-compressed
Output
MISP annotation and domain-ip objects with report context and authentication results
Requirements
PyMISP
Features
Upload an aggregate XML report (.xml, .xml.gz, or a ZIP containing exactly one XML file), or paste XML. Creates an annotation object with report metadata, published policy and the original XML attachment. Each aggregate record becomes a linked domain-ip object with its source IP (ip-src), header-from domain, reporting interval and a JSON text attribute preserving counts, disposition, SPF/DKIM results, identifiers and extension fields. Additional identifier and authentication domains are included for correlation. All attributes have to_ids disabled: DMARC observations do not by themselves identify malicious senders. No API key or network access is needed. Input and decompressed XML are limited to 20 MiB each, with at most 10,000 records and 32 XML nesting levels. DTDs, encrypted or multi-file ZIPs, nested archives and forensic/failure reports (RUF/ARF) are not supported. Invalid records reject the entire import.
References
https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7489.html https://github.com/MISP/misp-modules/issues/508

Accept DNS names, URLs, email addresses and IPs (reverse DNS). Query common mail-policy TXT names and optionally resolve discovered names to A/AAAA. Eight workers share a total time budget; failures retain successful results. See documentation/expansion/dns_query.json for configuration and limitations.

Import

Email Import

email_import

Email import module for MISP

Module details
Module Type
import
Input
E-mail file
Output
MISP Event attributes
Features
This module can be used to import e-mail text as well as attachments and urls. Configuration parameters are used to unzip attachments, guess zip attachment passwords, extract urls, remove common subject markers, and extract partial inline forwarded emails (extract_forwarded_emails, disabled by default): All switches default to False and accept JSON booleans, 0/1, and case-insensitive yes/no strings. ZIP extraction is limited per request to 100 members, 50 MiB expanded bytes, and 100 password candidates; each member is limited to 20 MiB. Originals are retained and skipped archives are reported. Forward extraction supports English From/To/Cc/Bcc/Reply-To/Sent/Date/Subject header blocks in plain text and HTML, including Outlook. Folded header values are supported. Each block needs a sender address, a subject, and a recipient or date. At most 20 partial email objects are linked to the carrier with includes references. Plain text is preferred; HTML is used if no forwards are found in plain text. Reconstructed attributes have to_ids disabled; the original email is retained as evidence. Local or unparseable timestamps are preserved as text in the reconstructed headers. Existing extract_urls and remove_subject_markers settings also apply to forwards. URL objects are shared between the carrier and forwards that contain the same URL. Submitted EML/MSG bytes are preserved separately from converted EML and heuristic forwards. See the [usage guide](https://github.com/MISP/misp-modules/blob/main/documentation/import_mod/email_import.md).
References
https://github.com/MISP/mail_to_misp

Event to PDF Export

Simple export of a MISP event to PDF.

Module details
Module Type
export
Input
MISP Event
Output
MISP Event in a PDF file.
Requirements
PyMISP reportlab
Features
The module takes care of the PDF file building, and work with any MISP Event. Except the requirement of reportlab, used to create the file, there is no special feature concerning the Event. Some parameters can be given through the config dict. 'MISP_base_url_for_dynamic_link' is your MISP URL, to attach an hyperlink to your event on your MISP instance from the PDF. Keep it clear to avoid hyperlinks in the generated pdf. 'MISP_name_for_metadata' is your CERT or MISP instance name. Used as text in the PDF' metadata 'Activate_textual_description' is a boolean (True or void) to activate the textual description/header abstract of an event 'Activate_galaxy_description' is a boolean (True or void) to activate the description of event related galaxies. 'Activate_related_events' is a boolean (True or void) to activate the description of related event. Be aware this might leak information on confidential events linked to the current event ! 'Activate_internationalization_fonts' is a boolean (True or void) to activate Noto fonts instead of default fonts (Helvetica). This allows the support of CJK alphabet. Be sure to have followed the procedure to download Noto fonts (~70Mo) in the right place (/tools/pdf_fonts/Noto_TTF), to allow PyMisp to find and use them during PDF generation. 'Custom_fonts_path' is a text (path or void) to the TTF file of your choice, to create the PDF with it. Be aware the PDF won't support bold/italic/special style anymore with this option
References
https://acrobat.adobe.com/us/en/acrobat/about-adobe-pdf.html

Expansion

Extuno Lookup

extuno

Query Extuno for the reputation of a browser extension, an IDE extension or a package, identified by its store id or its listing URL.

Module details
Module Type
expansion hover
Input
A store listing URL, or a text attribute holding `store:id` (e.g. `chrome:cjpalhd...`).
Output
A reputation object holding the Extuno verdict, its risk score and the advisory it came from.
Requirements
An Extuno API key
Features
The module takes a store listing URL, or a `store:id` pair in a text attribute, and reports what Extuno knows about that artifact: whether it appears in the known-malicious catalog, with the threat type and the advisory it came from, and whether Extuno's own static and sandbox analysis reached a verdict on it. It covers browser extensions (Chrome, Firefox, Edge), IDE extensions (VS Code, JetBrains, Eclipse), Discord client mods and the npm, PyPI, Packagist, Maven, WordPress and Open VSX registries. Browser and IDE extensions are the reason the module exists: they are not covered by OSV or any other public advisory database, so an extension id found on a workstation cannot be checked against one. Only the identifier being looked up leaves the MISP instance. The lookup is read-only and never submits the artifact for analysis.

Features
This module takes a domain, hostname or IP address MISP attribute as input to query the Farsight Passive DNS API. The results of rdata and rrset lookups are then returned and parsed into passive-dns objects. An API key is required to submit queries to the API. It is also possible to define a custom server URL, and to set a limit of results to get. This limit is set for each lookup, which means we can have an up to the limit number of passive-dns objects resulting from an rdata query about an IP address, but an up to the limit number of passive-dns objects for each lookup queries about a domain or a hostname (== twice the limit). SOA contact emails are also returned as dns-soa-email attributes. For unescaped mailbox names, the Public Suffix List is used to infer the email domain; this is a heuristic. Raw SOA records are preserved.

Export

GoAML Export

goamlexport

This module is used to export MISP events containing transaction objects into GoAML format.

Module details
Module Type
export
Input
MISP objects (transaction, bank-account, person, legal-entity, geolocation), with references, describing financial transactions and their origin and target.
Output
GoAML format file, describing financial transactions, with their origin and target (bank accounts, persons or entities).
Requirements
PyMISP MISP objects
Features
The module works as long as there is at least one transaction object in the Event. Then in order to have a valid GoAML document, please follow these guidelines: - For each transaction object, use either a bank-account, person, or legal-entity object to describe the origin of the transaction, and again one of them to describe the target of the transaction. - Create an object reference for both origin and target objects of the transaction. - A bank-account object needs a signatory, which is a person object, put as object reference of the bank-account. - A person can have an address, which is a geolocation object, put as object reference of the person. Supported relation types for object references that are recommended for each object are the folowing: - transaction: - 'from', 'from_my_client': Origin of the transaction - at least one of them is required. - 'to', 'to_my_client': Target of the transaction - at least one of them is required. - 'address': Location of the transaction - optional. - bank-account: - 'signatory': Signatory of a bank-account - the reference from bank-account to a signatory is required, but the relation-type is optional at the moment since this reference will always describe a signatory. - 'entity': Entity owning the bank account - optional. - person: - 'address': Address of a person - optional.
References
http://goaml.unodc.org/
Author
Christian Studer
Version
1

Private, reserved and mixed public/private DNS answers are rejected. No proxy or browser is used. max_size_mb defaults to 5 (1-25), enforced while streaming content. HTML is converted into Markdown; PDFs are preserved. Returns a page-capture object referencing the URL attribute.

IPGeolocation.io Lookup

ipgeolocation

An expansion and hover module to enrich an IP address with geolocation, ASN, company, threat intelligence (threat score, VPN, proxy, Tor, bot and spam signals) and abuse contact information from IPGeolocation.io, either through the API or from local IPGeolocation.io MMDB databases.

Module details
Module Type
expansion hover
Input
An IP address attribute (ip-src, ip-dst, ip-src|port, ip-dst|port or domain|ip).
Output
geolocation, asn and domain-ip objects, and an ipgeolocation-ip object with the threat score, anonymisation signals, company and abuse contact.
Requirements
An IPGeolocation.io API key, or IPGeolocation.io MMDB databases stored on the misp-modules host
Features
The module takes an IP address attribute as input and answers from one of two sources: - `api_key`: the [IPGeolocation.io API](https://ipgeolocation.io/documentation/ip-location-api.html). Free plans return geolocation and ASN. Paid plans also return the company, threat intelligence (`include=security`), the abuse contact (`include=abuse`) and the hostname; the `include` setting chooses these modules (default `security,abuse,hostname`, `none` for the base lookup only). If the plan does not allow them, the module falls back to the base lookup. Results are cached in memory for `cache_ttl` seconds (default 3600) to save credits on repeated lookups such as hover. - `mmdb_paths`: comma-separated `.mmdb` files or directories of IPGeolocation.io databases: Location, Country, ISP, ASN, Company, Abuse Contact, Security (all versions), Residential Proxy and Hosting, or their combined editions. Names are returned in English. Lookups run locally and nothing is sent to IPGeolocation.io, which suits air-gapped instances and indicators that must not leave the organisation. Several databases are combined; for a field present in more than one, the first file in the list wins. Updated files are picked up automatically within a minute. When `mmdb_paths` is set, the API is never called.
References
https://ipgeolocation.io/documentation/ip-location-api.html https://ipgeolocation.io/ip-security-database.html

Explicit false flags are retained; absent fields do not imply a clean address. Hosted domains included in the response are added to the domain-ip object. No additional API endpoints are queried.

Expansion

Malwagon Lookup

malwagon

Look up a SHA256 digest in the Malwagon sandbox and return the scans it already has for it.

Module details
Module Type
expansion hover
Input
A sha256 or filename|sha256 attribute.
Output
A file object for the sample and one sandbox-report object per Malwagon analysis, with the verdict expressed as MISP taxonomy tags.
Requirements
A Malwagon API key with the read scope.
Features
The module takes a sha256 or filename|sha256 attribute and asks Malwagon which analyses it already holds for that digest. The lookup is free and answers immediately, so it is safe to use on hover: no sample leaves the MISP instance and no detonation quota is spent. Only the digest is sent. Each analysis comes back as a sandbox-report object carrying the verdict, the score and a permalink to the report, referenced from a file object for the sample. The verdict is translated into MISP's own vocabulary - a misp:threat-level tag, plus ioc:artifact-state where the verdict is conclusive - rather than being passed through as a vendor string. To detonate something Malwagon has never seen, use the Malwagon Submit module instead.
References
https://malwagon.com https://malwagon.com/docs/api https://www.misp-project.org/taxonomies.html
Author

Expansion

Malwagon Submit

malwagon_submit

Detonate a sample or a URL in the Malwagon sandbox and return the analysis.

Module details
Module Type
expansion
Input
An attachment, malware-sample or url attribute.
Output
A file object for the sample and a sandbox-report object for the Malwagon analysis, with the verdict expressed as MISP taxonomy tags.
Requirements
A Malwagon API key with the submit scope.
Features
The module takes an attachment, malware-sample or url attribute and detonates it in the Malwagon sandbox. A malware-sample arrives zip-encrypted with the password infected and is unpacked before submission. A file is looked up by its SHA256 first. If Malwagon has already analysed that digest the existing analysis is returned, which is free, instant, and spends no detonation quota; set always_submit to force a fresh detonation instead. The module then polls the scan until it finishes or until poll_timeout seconds have passed, and returns what it has either way, so a long detonation gives back a permalink rather than an error. This module submits the sample itself to a third party, so it is deliberately expansion-only and never runs on hover. Submission is blocked when the attribute carries a TLP tag more restrictive than max_tlp, and scans are created private unless private is set to false. The sandbox image is chosen by the platform from the sample; on the free and community tiers the analysis virtual machine has no internet access at all, which is structural rather than a quota, so network-dependent samples will look inert there.
References
https://malwagon.com https://malwagon.com/docs/api https://www.misp-project.org/taxonomies.html
Author
Tolga Sezer

Expansion

NetAPI Lookup

netapi

Check a domain, hostname, URL or IP address against the NetAPI compromised feeds and get the domain's position in the NetAPI Top 1M.

Module details
Module Type
expansion hover
Input
A domain, hostname, URL or IP address.
Output
A reputation object with the feed listing and, for a domain, the Top 1M rank.
Features
The module takes a domain, hostname, URL (by its host) or IP address attribute and queries the free compromised-check method of the NetAPI JSON API. For a domain or hostname it says whether the value, or the registered domain a hostname belongs to, is in the NetAPI feed of hosts that public threat feeds report for malware or phishing: listed now (seen within the last 24 hours), listed in the past only, or never listed, with the first and last seen dates, the reporting feed and the registrar of the domain. A second free method, domain-rank, gives the position of the registered domain in the NetAPI Top 1M, a daily popularity ranking: a top-ranked domain in the feed is more likely a compromised legitimate site than infrastructure set up by the attacker. For an IP address it checks the NetAPI compromised IP feed, the IPv4 addresses that attacked the sensors of NetAPI Nightwatch, NetAPI's own honeypot network: listed now (seen within the last 48 hours), listed in the past only, or never listed, with the first seen date, the time of the last attack and the type of attack. Private, loopback and reserved addresses are not sent. The answer is a reputation object linked to the queried attribute: classification malicious when the value is listed now, suspicious when only its registered domain is, and unknown when it is listed in the past only or never (the feed holds no opinion on a value it does not list), with the first and last seen dates, a link to the NetAPI domain or IP lookup and the details (for a domain also the Top 1M rank) in its text. No API key is required. An optional NetAPI API token only raises the request limits (30 requests a minute and 1,000 a day per IP address without one). Only the queried indicator leaves the MISP instance.
References
https://netapi.com/compromised-urls/ https://netapi.com/compromised-ips/ https://netapi.com/top-1-mln-websites/ https://netapi.com/help/api/#json-api
Author

OpenCTI Lookup

opencti

Query an OpenCTI instance for exact observable matches and their context and source references.

Module details
Note
Input/output attributes are computed dynamically; see source.
Module Type
expansion
Input
A domain, hostname, IP address, URL, email address or file hash (including filename|hash).
Output
MISP text and link attributes with provenance and TLP tags.
Requirements
requests An OpenCTI instance and an API token with knowledge read access.
Features
Read-only GraphQL lookup using OpenCTI's FilterGroup API (OpenCTI 5.12 or later). Set url to the instance base URL (optionally ending in /graphql) and token to its API token. max_results defaults to 20 (1-100) and timeout to 30 seconds (1-120). Domains and IPs are normalized; file hashes, including filename|hash attributes, are matched against the specific hash algorithm. Results contain text context (description, score, author, labels, markings and timestamps), links to OpenCTI and external references. Imported attributes have to_ids=false; TLP markings are retained as tags and other markings as text. Custom markings and OpenCTI access controls are not translated into MISP sharing restrictions. No data is written to OpenCTI and no relationship traversal or synchronization is performed. A result cap notice is returned when more matches are available. No matches produce an empty Attribute list.
References
https://docs.opencti.io/latest/reference/api/

Features
A backup import path for legacy .ioc files after removal of the core OpenIOC importer in MISP 3.0. Upload an OpenIOC 1.0 (ioc/definition) or 1.1 (OpenIOC/criteria) XML file through Import from modules, using openiocimport. Common file, network, email, registry, mutex and service fields become MISP attributes; unmapped fields are retained as other attributes. The original XML is attached by default; the existing not save ioc and default tag options are supported. XML DTDs and custom entities are rejected. This extracts observables, rather than evaluating OpenIOC rules: conditions, negation, case sensitivity, item IDs and the AND/OR group path are recorded in attribute comments. All attributes have to_ids=false for review. Correlation is disabled for grouped AND terms, non-exact or negated conditions and unmapped fields, so these are not treated as independent exact indicators. Keep the attachment for the full rule.

PCAP Import

pcap_import

Import a PCAP or PCAPNG capture, including reassembled files, emails and network indicators.

Module details
Module Type
import
Input
Base64-encoded PCAP or PCAPNG file
Output
MISP network attributes, pcap-metadata, network-connection, file and email objects with capture/stream provenance
Requirements
TShark >= 4.0 on the service user's PATH (Debian/Ubuntu: apt install tshark) PyMISP with email and fileobjects extras (included in misp-modules[all])
Features
Parses captures offline with TShark, without capture privileges or network lookups. Extracts IPv4/IPv6 endpoints, DNS names and answers, HTTP URLs, hosts and user agents, and TLS SNI hostnames. Reassembles HTTP files and SMTP messages; reuses email_import for email objects, attachments and body URLs. Requires complete, unencrypted application traffic for payload extraction; HTTPS yields visible TLS metadata only. Other file-transfer protocols and TLS decryption are not supported. Observed network attributes have to_ids disabled for analyst review. Captures are limited to 50 MiB, exported data and JSON metadata to 100 MiB each. timeout is a positive number of seconds, at most 300 (default 60). Output sizes, including diagnostics, are checked every 50 ms while TShark runs; exceeding a limit kills the process. Bursts can overshoot between checks; these checks are not filesystem quotas. Adds capture hashes and pcap-metadata, capture-scoped TCP/UDP network-connection objects, packet timestamps and observation intervals. Reconstructed content links to streams by exact payload hashes; identical content retains all observed sources. SMTP provenance uses a targeted second pass within the same timeout and combined metadata limit. See the [usage guide](https://github.com/MISP/misp-modules/blob/main/documentation/import_mod/pcap_import.md).
References
https://github.com/MISP/misp-modules/issues/397 https://www.wireshark.org/docs/man-pages/tshark.html

Search and retrieval are bounded; individual retrieval failures retain index metadata with an object comment. Keyserver UIDs and flags are unverified claims; signatures and ownership are not validated. pgp-message is provided for message artifacts linked to pgp-meta; this module does not retrieve or decrypt messages. Configuration: keyserver, timeout (default 10 seconds per HTTP request), max_results (default 10, maximum 100). New object templates are bundled for older PyMISP versions. Enable extract_signatures to return pgp-sign objects with the original signature packets, issuer IDs and fingerprints, signature metadata and UID/subkey context. max_signatures limits signature objects across the lookup (default 100, maximum 1000). Issuer claims are preserved without verification.

PTR Classification

ptrclassify

Classify PTR hostnames and tag queried attributes with the ptrclassify taxonomy.

Module details
Module Type
expansion hover
Input
An ip-src, ip-dst, domain|ip, hostname or domain attribute.
Output
The tagged input attribute, one ptrclassify object per hostname, and a dns-record object for IP lookups.
Requirements
ptrclassify and dnspython Python libraries; DNS access for IP lookups
Features
IPv4 and IPv6 attributes are reverse-resolved and every distinct PTR hostname is classified locally using ptrclassify's built-in rules, retaining the queried address to detect IP-encoded naming. Hostname and domain attributes are classified directly, without DNS or an API key. Matching ptrclassify taxonomy tags are added to the queried attribute, retaining its UUID and existing tags, and to PTR answers in a `dns-record` object. One `ptrclassify` object per hostname holds the classification labels, confidence, evidence, rule IDs and potential location hints. Repeated classification fields share the machine tag as their attribute comment; location fields share a rule-ID/code comment. Classification objects reference the queried attribute and, for IP lookups, the DNS object. No match returns an object with `matched=0` without adding tags. Configure `nameserver` to use a specific DNS server; otherwise the system resolver is used. DNS lookups have a five-second lifetime. Classification is heuristic: PTR names are operator-controlled, and inferred locations are hints, not verified geolocation. Hover displays the enrichment; importing the expansion applies the returned tags in MISP. Enable the ptrclassify taxonomy in MISP to manage these tags, and install the ptrclassify MISP object template. The module bundles the template so it also works with PyMISP versions that do not yet include it.
References
https://github.com/adulau/ptrclassify https://misp-project.org/taxonomies.html#_ptrclassify

Expansion

Sherlock Lookup

sherlock

Find social media accounts by username with Sherlock.

Module details
Module Type
expansion hover
Input
A target-user, github-username, text, or email attribute. A leading @ on a username is removed.
Output
One user-account object per match, with username, platform, profile link and a reference to the input.
Requirements
Install the sherlock-project CLI separately (for example: pipx install sherlock-project). No API key required.
Features
Runs the Sherlock CLI and returns user-account objects for claimed usernames only. Text is searched as a single literal username, without extracting names or generating variants. Email input uses the local part before @ as a candidate username; matches do not verify email ownership or identity. Install Sherlock for the misp-modules service user and put sherlock on its PATH, or set sherlock_path to the executable's absolute path (not a shell command). Optional sites is a comma-separated list of Sherlock site names; github-username defaults to GitHub only. timeout is the per-site timeout in seconds (default 10); scan_timeout bounds the whole process (default 120). Both must be positive finite numbers. Keep scan_timeout below the MISP enrichment and module-server request timeouts, or raise those timeouts for broad searches. Sherlock contacts the selected sites and downloads its current site definitions. Start misp-modules with --debug to log the command, live CLI output, elapsed time and report summary; this also enables Sherlock's --verbose output. --debug-extended HTTP tracing runs in the server process and cannot trace Sherlock's separate process. For troubleshooting, first limit sites to GitHub. Results can contain false positives and should be reviewed.
References
https://github.com/sherlock-project/sherlock https://sherlockproject.xyz/usage

requests PyMISP

Query the SoChain API v3 for a btc attribute or a coin-address object. A btc attribute is looked up on Bitcoin. A coin-address object is looked up on the network named by its symbol (BTC, LTC, DOGE or ZEC); without a symbol, the network is the first of Bitcoin, Litecoin, Dogecoin and Zcash on which SoChain says the address is valid. The result is a coin-address object with the balance, total received and sent, the number of transactions and the first and last activity, referencing the input. Recent counterparties are returned as coin-address objects linked with `paid` references (5 on hover, 50 when the magnifying glass is clicked), whose comments give the amount, transaction and block. When look-alike addresses sent the address dust to poison its history, each one is returned as a coin-address object that `impersonates` the address it copies. No API key is needed for up to 2,500 lookups a day per IP. With a key from https://sochain.com/dashboard, lookups count against that account's plan.

A shortened-link object referencing the original URL attribute.

urllib3 certifi idna PyMISP Direct outbound HTTP(S) and DNS access

Resolve known shorteners and optional additional_shorteners (comma-separated exact hostnames). Follow at most max_redirects HTTP redirects (default 10, maximum 20), using HEAD with streamed GET fallback on HTTP 405/501. timeout is per request (default 10 seconds, maximum 30); DNS uses the system resolver. Generated attributes have to_ids=false.

requests pymisp

Boolean options accept true/false or their string equivalents. Unset options (null or blank strings from MISP) use their documented defaults. The request's top-level timeout limits total module execution independently of config.timeout. CPE lookup uses cpe_source (default cvelistv5) and cpe_page (default 1). Results match vendor and product; exact version applicability must be checked. CPE search imports advisories from one bounded page; the optional community and priority lookups apply to vulnerability ID input. Original advisory JSON is retained as a base64 payload; community, EPSS and KEV records retain JSON attachments. Unavailable optional data does not discard the advisory. The companion vulnerability-sighting, epss-score and known-exploited-vulnerability templates are bundled for compatibility with existing PyMISP releases.

xposedornot

Query the XposedOrNot API to check whether an email address appears in known data breaches.

Module details
Module Type
expansion hover
Input
An email address.
Output
One breach object per data breach the email address appears in.
Requirements
No API key required.
Features
The module takes an email address as input and queries the XposedOrNot API to determine whether the address appears in known data breaches. Each exposure is returned as a breach object holding the breach name, date, number of exposed records, affected domain, exposed data classes and password storage risk. Without any configuration the free keyless API is used (rate limits apply: 2 requests/second, 25/hour per IP); an optional commercial api_key switches to the higher-limit Plus API. The queried email address is sent over TLS to xposedornot.com; nothing else leaves the MISP instance.

yara-python python library
Features
Produces a ZIP of unchanged stored YARA collections in separate namespaces, with a provenance and exclusion manifest. The default both mode exports yara attributes regardless of to_ids and generates literal, case-sensitive UTF-8 byte searches from supported IDS-marked attributes. Select rules or indicators to export only stored collections or generated IOC searches, respectively. A filename or domain matches bytes in scanned content, not a file's name or DNS activity. ZoomEye

zoomeye

Search ZoomEye API v2 for IP addresses, domains, hostnames and SHA-1 certificate fingerprints.

Module details
Module Type
expansion
Input
ip-src, ip-dst, domain, hostname, x509-fingerprint-sha1 MISP attribute.
Output
Referenced ip-port objects and an annotation with result count and search coverage.
Requirements
requests ZoomEye API key
Features
Requires `api_key`. Builds an escaped, Base64-encoded search query for API v2 and requests one page of up to `max_results` assets (default 20, maximum 100). Uses the v4/v6 dataset for IPs, web for domains, and all datasets for hostnames and certificate fingerprints. Leading/trailing API key whitespace is removed. A result-limit notice is included when total exceeds the returned records; additional pages are not fetched automatically. Returns referenced ip-port objects with service/banner context, and an annotation retaining result counts and observed metadata. Certificate searches identify assets using an observed certificate, not a malicious verdict. All enrichment has to_ids disabled.
